dedupe_keys.name: locations along the czech railway network with the highest tree fall hazard 2012 2015 events

description: This study identifies the segments of the Czech railway network with the highest hazard of trees falling onto tracks or overhead lines, one of the most common natural causes of disruption. The authors analysed 2,039 tree-fall events registered between 2012 and 2015, some with up to 70 trees; 32 percent were caused by 14 weather extremes with more than 20 concurrent events, and 12 derailments due to fallen trees occurred in the period. They combined event data with land use and track data from OpenStreetMap, computed hazard with a generalised rule of succession and clustered events, finding 59 of 2,960 segments with the highest hazard and 267 clusters for priority vegetation monitoring. Coverage: the Czech national rail network. Format and access: open access article in Applied Geography (2017). Licence and cost: CC BY-NC-ND, free to read. Caveats: the event records belong to the rail manager and are not published with the article. It supports hazard exposure and resilience studies of lineside vegetation. It relates to the Sachsenwald railway tree fall mapping case, OpenStreetMap and OpenRailwayMap in the catalogue.
